knowledge:
- key_parameters: organism=The KEGG organism code (e.g., "hsa", "mmu", "dre") used to build the graph ;; filter.path=Vector of KEGG pathway IDs to exclude (typically broad overview pathways like "01100") ;; databaseDir=Character string specifying the local directory where the KEGG database is built or loaded ;; matrices=Specifies which matrices to compute or load ("none", "diffusion", "pagerank") ;; normality=Specifies for which methods to compute the analytical null distribution ("diffusion", "pagerank") ;; compounds=Vector of affected KEGG compound IDs provided by the user ;; method=Enrichment method to run ("hypergeom", "diffusion", "pagerank", or a list of them) ;; approx=Statistical approximation method ("normality" for fast analytical z-scores, "simulation" for Monte Carlo trials) ;; threshold=P-score significance threshold for filtering results in tables, graphs, or plots ;; nlimit=Maximum number of nodes to display in plots or export in graphs
- alternatives: Over-representation analysis (classical hypergeometric test on pathways alone). FELLA includes a hypergeometric test (method = "hypergeom") for comparison, but its main strength lies in the network-based diffusion and PageRank methods which incorporate network topology and contextual biological entities.
- when_to_use: When you have a list of affected metabolites (KEGG compound IDs) from an experimental contrast and want to identify not just enriched pathways, but also the intermediate reactions, enzymes, and modules that connect them in a coherent biological subgraph.
- pitfalls: Do not manually modify the database internal files or FELLA.DATA slots to avoid corruption. Always build FELLA.USER objects using defineCompounds or enrich rather than manipulating slots manually to ensure quality checks are run. Exact matching is required for compound IDs; whitespaces, tabs, or incorrect prefixes will cause mismatches and exclusions. buildDataFromGraph will raise an error if the target database directory already exists and contains a database; the user must delete or unlink the existing directory first.

workflows.name: kegg_network_enrichment
workflows.intent: Build a local KEGG database for a specific organism, map a list of affected metabolites, perform network-based enrichment (diffusion or PageRank), and export/visualize the resulting subnetwork.
input: list_of_compounds.txt (A character vector of affected KEGG compound IDs)
workflows.stages: 1. Build the KEGG graph from KEGGREST using buildGraphFromKEGGREST. 2. Build the local database files using buildDataFromGraph. 3. Load the KEGG database using loadKEGGdata. 4. Define and map the affected compounds using defineCompounds. 5. Run enrichment analysis using runDiffusion or enrich. 6. Visualize the enriched subnetwork using plot. 7. Export results as a table using generateResultsTable or exportResults. 8. Export results as an igraph object using generateResultsGraph. 9. (Optional) Annotate the graph with GO terms using addGOToGraph.
workflows.code:
graph <- buildGraphFromKEGGREST(
    organism = "mmu", 
    filter.path = c("01100", "01200", "01210", "01212", "01230"))

tmpdir <- paste0(tempdir(), "/my_database")
unlink(tmpdir, recursive = TRUE)  
buildDataFromGraph(
    keggdata.graph = graph, 
    databaseDir = tmpdir, 
    internalDir = FALSE, 
    matrices = "none", 
    normality = "diffusion", 
    niter = 100)

fella.data <- loadKEGGdata(
    databaseDir = tmpdir, 
    internalDir = FALSE, 
    loadMatrix = "none"
)

cpd.nafld <- c(
    "C00020", # AMP
    "C00719", # Betaine
    "C00114", # Choline
    "C00037", # Glycine
    "C00160", # Glycolate
    "C01104"  # Trimethylamine-N-oxide
)

analysis.nafld <- enrich(
    compounds = cpd.nafld, 
    data = fella.data, 
    method = "diffusion", 
    approx = "normality")

plot(
    analysis.nafld, 
    method = "diffusion", 
    data = fella.data, 
    nlimit = 250,  
    plotLegend = FALSE)

g.nafld <-  generateResultsGraph(
    object = analysis.nafld, 
    data = fella.data, 
    method = "diffusion")

tab.all <- generateResultsTable(
    method = "diffusion", 
    nlimit = 100, 
    object = analysis.nafld, 
    data = fella.data)

tmpfile <- tempfile()
exportResults(
    format = "csv", 
    file = tmpfile, 
    method = "diffusion", 
    object = analysis.nafld, 
    data = fella.data)

g.go <- addGOToGraph(
    graph = g.nafld, 
    GOterm = "GO:0005739", 
    godata.options = list(
        OrgDb = "org.Hs.eg.db", ont = "CC"), 
    mart.options = list(
        biomart = "ensembl", dataset = "hsapiens_gene_ensembl"))
